verdict.rationale: NotebookLM's core interaction is a chat interface where users ask natural-language questions to get grounded answers and can customize response style with free-text instructions (e.g., 'Respond like a PhD student') [notebooklm-docs-2, notebooklm-docs-28, notebooklm-docs-30]. However, most other actions—generating audio/video overviews, mind maps, flashcards, slide decks, source selection—are triggered via UI buttons/menus rather than natural-language commands, so the product is not fully operable end-to-end via NL. Missing for 10: evidence of NL commands controlling non-chat features (e.g., 'create a slide deck' via typed command), agentic multi-step NL orchestration, and independent confirmation that command-style control works reliably.
